note: Authoritative dataset registry. LIVE ADDRESS TODAY: each entry's `schema` and `name` are its address: `<schema>.<name>` in SQL, and `<name>` on the web (`/datasets/<name>`) and as the R2 file name (`<name>.parquet`). `schemas` lists the schemas the catalogue uses now. `moves_to` is the `<namespace>/<name>` address the entry takes at the cutover, the move of the catalogue and then the web; it is not live before then. At the cutover the entry takes its `moves_to` address and its old address joins `aliases` as `<schema>.<name>` (for example `source.gleif`). ADDRESS FROM THE CUTOVER: a dataset is addressed by a namespace and a name: `<namespace>/<name>` on the web, in files and on R2 (from the cutover, `/datasets/gleif/lei` and `gleif/lei.parquet`), and `<namespace>.<name>` in SQL (from the cutover, `meridian.gleif.lei`, where `meridian` is the alias the docs give the attached catalogue). The namespace says who holds the dataset; the name says which dataset it is. Both are lowercase snake_case, `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`. NAMESPACES (the `namespaces` object) are of three kinds. `held`: an issuer namespace, kept by Meridian on behalf of the organisation named under `issuer` until that organisation claims it; a claim hands over the namespace with the datasets and Protocols in it, and `claimed` records the state. `registered`: a namespace owned by the person, group or organisation that registered it, with its owner's own promise (none yet). `library`: Meridian's curated set, for core datasets that have no issuing organisation to hold a namespace for and for data Meridian makes itself. PROMISES: a managed Protocol (the arcform.yaml build recipe) promises the operations inside it, not the data: Meridian keeps the recipe working against the source it names. A managed Dataset promises that the dataset is available: hosted, refreshed at a stated interval and readable. `library` and each held namespace (until claimed) carry the promise that fits the entry, a Protocol's for a Protocol and a Dataset's for a hosted dataset; a name in either does not change, and an entry is retired only with notice and a successor. INVARIANTS: (1) `uid` is stable, opaque, and NEVER shown as an address; (2) a `uid` maps to exactly one dataset and is NEVER reused; (3) a retired slug is NEVER re-pointed at a different dataset; (4) a retired namespace or name is NEVER reissued, with one exception: a retired flat slug may become the namespace of the dataset it addressed (here `gleif`), and its old web path redirects to `<namespace>/<name>`; (5) a name in `reserved` cannot be registered as a new namespace. ON A RENAME, which the cutover is: keep `uid`, move the old address into `aliases`, emit a 301 (web) + a compatibility VIEW at the old name (SQL). The old R2 files are not redirected: each old flat file (`gleif.parquet`, `edgar.parquet`, `naics.parquet`, `edgar_gleif.parquet`) is frozen at the cutover, stays readable and is no longer overwritten, and each old manifest key keeps its last content-addressed `.url`. The 301s stay, except `/datasets/gleif`, which gives way to GLEIF's namespace page once GLEIF has a second dataset. The compatibility views, the frozen flat files and the old manifest keys are retired after a stated window, at least 90 days from the later of the cutover and the Brightfield release that stops reading the old addresses. Data VERSIONS are a separate axis, handled by the content-addressed `<sha>.parquet` + manifest pointer. Each entry also carries a `protocol` pointer to its arcform.yaml build recipe (how it is made) — null until authored. RESERVED (the `reserved` list): `library`, `meridian`, each held namespace, each registered namespace (it joins the list when it is registered, so the name cannot be registered a second time), the schema names the catalogue uses now or holds during the move (`main`, `source`, `crosswalk`), DuckDB's system schemas (`information_schema`, `pg_catalog`), the flat slugs the cutover retires that are not held namespaces (`edgar`, `naics`, `edgar_gleif`), and the words the routes use (`new`, `edit`, `search`).

schemas.source: Raw ingested reference data, one namespace per what-it-is.
schemas.crosswalk: Derived joins between datasets — the materialised relationships (the product).
